answer: A name cannot be bought with a lump stake. Entry follows a spiral of five cooling intervals, each a fifth shorter, and every turn demands a quartz tick: a signed energy receipt from a different physical host whose clock skew and thermal fingerprint disagree with the last. Between ticks the receipt sits in a velvet delay, a randomized twelve-hour quiet when no sibling host may speak. Shared fingerprints or talk through that velvet delay reset the spiral and lock the stake for two epochs. Datacenter clones share heat and fail the second turn.
